paper.title: Provably Efficient Online Hyperparameter Optimization with Population-Based Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Parallel (batch) time-varying Gaussian process bandit optimization (online hyperparameter schedule selection)
unmapped: Time-varying GP model of Bogunovic et al.: f_1 = g_1, f_{t+1} = sqrt(1-omega) f_t + sqrt(omega) g_{t+1}, g_i i.i.d. GP(0,k); forgetting parameter omega
Batch of B parallel agents per round; regret per round is that of the best agent in the batch (min over b)
The learner knows the time-varying kernel including omega, and the constants a, b, r used in beta_T
settings.definition_quote: We formulate this problem as optimizing the time-varying black-box reward function $f_t$, over $\mathcal{D}$. Every $t_{\mathrm{ready}}$ steps, we observe and record noisy observations, $y_t = f_t(x_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2\mathbf{I})$ ... f_{t+1}(x) = \sqrt{1-\omega}f_t(x) + \sqrt{\omega}g_{t+1}(x)

bound.regime: any block length N_tilde in {1,...,T}, B << T

symbols.beta_T: 2 log(pi^2 T^2/(2 delta)) + 2 d log(r d b T^2 sqrt(log(d a pi^2 T^2/(2 delta))))
symbols.gamma_NB: maximum information gain of the (time-invariant) kernel after N_tilde*B_pop points
symbols.omega: forgetting parameter of the time-varying GP

conditions: domain D subset of [0,r]^d compact and convex
f_t ~ GP(0,k) almost surely continuously differentiable
Lipschitz assumption: P(sup |df_t/dx^(j)| >= L_t) <= a exp(-(L_t/b)^2) for some a, b
tuning: beta_T = 2 log(pi^2 T^2/(2 delta)) + 2 d log(r d b T^2 sqrt(log(d a pi^2 T^2/(2 delta))))

source.quote: Let the domain $\mathcal{D}\subset[0,r]^{d}$ be compact and convex ... Pick $\delta\in(0,1)$, set $\beta_{T}=2\log\frac{\pi^{2}T^{2}}{2\delta}+2d\log rdbT^{2}\sqrt{\log\frac{da\pi^{2}T^{2}}{2\delta}}$ and define $C_{1}=32/\log(1+\sigma_{f}^{2})$, the PB2 algorithm satisfies the following regret bound after $T$ time steps over $B$ parallel agents with probability at least $1-\delta$: R_{TB}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}f_{t}(\bx_{t}^{*})-\max_{b} f_{t}(\bx_{t,b})\le \sqrt{C_{1}T\beta_{T}(\frac{T}{\tilde{N}B}+1)(\gamma_{\tilde{N}B}+[\tilde{N}B]^{3}\omega)}+2 the bound holds for any block length $\tilde{N}\in\{1,...,T\}$ and $B\ll T$.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 12 (label main_theorem) in the appendix with identical bound. The proof's final line actually has T/B instead of T and a 1/sigma_f^2 factor on the omega term, and C_1 is defined inconsistently (log(1+sigma_f^2) vs log(1+sigma_f^{-2})); recorded the statement as printed. Regret per round is f_t(x*_t) minus the best of B batch points, against per-round maximiser. Proof also specialises to SE kernel with gamma = O((log N_tilde B)^{d+1}); not recorded separately. Time-varying GP drift via omega mapped to nonstationary_drifting.
